post.description: Requires a browser session or a personal token with gifts:write. Records a debt the person owes or is owed: `amount` is a decimal string and `currencyCode` a three-letter code the workspace supports. A debt created settled may carry a settlement reason and the file id of a settlement photo, which must be an available JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of this same person in this workspace; a token needs no files scope to reference it. An optional `requestId` (a UUID the client generates once per intended record) makes a retry safe: repeating the request with the same `requestId` and the same payload returns the record the first attempt wrote, answering 201 again without writing anything; the same `requestId` with a different payload, or for a different person, answers 409 `gift_request_conflict`; and once that record was deleted, the same `requestId` answers 409 `gift_request_deleted` rather than recording it again. The key is the workspace's, shared by every member and token. A workspace reset removes the audit history together with the records, so after a reset the same `requestId` creates the record again. Without `requestId`, repeating the request records a second debt. An archived person's gifts and debts can be read but refuse this write.

patch.description: Requires a browser session or a personal token with gifts:write. Edits a debt's `amount`, `currencyCode`, `direction`, or `reason`; status moves with changeDebtStatus. A field left out keeps its value, `reason: null` clears the reason, and at least one field must be named. `expectedUpdatedAt` is required: the debt's `updatedAt` from listPersonGiftsAndDebts or the last write; when the debt has changed since, it answers 409 `gift_stale` and changes nothing. The amount, currency, and direction can change only while the debt is open and has never been settled, because its settlement history records what was paid; once it has been settled, even if reopened since, they answer 409 `debt_values_locked`, and its reason stays editable. A cancelled debt is finished and refuses every edit with 409 `debt_values_locked`. A debt a recurring rule charged is an ordinary debt once charged: editing it changes neither the rule nor its other charges, and the rule never charges that period again. A request that changes nothing answers `unchanged`. A debt under another person's path answers 404. An archived person's gifts and debts can be read but refuse this write.

patch.description: Requires a browser session or a personal token with gifts:write. Settling appends to the debt's permanent settlement history and may carry a reason and the file id of a settlement photo, which must be an available JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of this same person in this workspace; a token needs no files scope to reference it. Asking for the status the debt already has answers `unchanged`. An optional `expectedUpdatedAt`, the debt's `updatedAt` from listPersonGiftsAndDebts or the last write, makes the change conditional: when the debt has changed since, it answers 409 `gift_stale` and changes nothing, so no settlement is recorded; without it the change applies to whatever the debt is now. patch.description: Requires a browser session or a personal token with gifts:write. Edits a gift's values: `name`, `amount` with `currencyCode`, `eventAt`, `comment`, `url`, `recipientPersonId`, and `attachmentFileId` — what createGift accepts except `status`, which changeGiftStatus moves. A field left out keeps its value and `null` clears an optional one; `name` cannot be cleared, and at least one field must be named. `amount` and `currencyCode` are sent together or not at all, and an amount needs a currency the workspace supports. `expectedUpdatedAt` is required: the gift's `updatedAt` from listPersonGiftsAndDebts or the last write; when the gift has changed since, it answers 409 `gift_stale` and changes nothing. A `comment` longer than 10,000 characters or a `url` longer than 2,000 answers 400 and changes nothing, as on createGift. A recipient must be a live person of this workspace. An attachment must be an available file of this workspace that is not a person's avatar; it replaces the gift's attachment, `null` removes it, and either way the previous file stays in the person's files. post.description: Requires a browser session or a personal token with gifts:write. Creates a rule that charges the person the same debt every period. Every period already due in the workspace's calendar is charged at once, one open debt per period. `amount` is a decimal string and `currencyCode` a three-letter code the workspace supports. An optional `requestId` (a UUID the client generates once per intended rule) makes a retry safe: the same `requestId` and payload returns the rule the first attempt created, answering 201 with `charged: 0` because the periods that attempt charged are never charged again; a different payload or person answers 409 `gift_request_conflict`; and once the rule was deleted it answers 409 `gift_request_deleted` and charges nothing. A workspace reset removes the audit history together with the records, so after a reset the same `requestId` creates the rule again and charges its due periods. Without `requestId`, repeating the request creates a second rule and charges its due periods again. An archived person's gifts and debts can be read but refuse this write.

It changes its title, anchorOn, sendTime, recurrenceUnit, or recurrenceInterval, at least one of them. Read the person's reminders first (listPersonReminders) and send that reminder's updatedAt as expectedUpdatedAt; a reminder changed since answers 409 reminder_stale. Its unattempted future occurrences are replaced from the new schedule, exactly as disabling and re-enabling it would, and in the same request every member who had occurrences of it gets the new schedule's occurrences, each in their own time zone and on their own delivery channels. Delivered and in-flight occurrences are kept as they are; an occurrence already retrying after a failed attempt keeps its remaining retries under the time and title it was minted with; a disabled reminder stays disabled. A reminder generated from an important date answers 409 reminder_managed_by_source: change the date on the person instead. Archived people are read-only. Does not grant read access.
